key_insight: A structured, ten-step LLM-assisted workflow can support machine-checked verification of complex algorithms in Dafny while shifting human effort toward supervision and specification review.
engineering_relevance: Combining LLM-generated proofs with automated testing, verifier feedback, and performance profiling offers a practical route to verifying sophisticated scientific software.
method: Formalize algorithms and develop contracts with human oversight.
Empirically validate invariants and iteratively construct proofs using verification feedback.
Profile verification bottlenecks and optimize proofs around solver resource demands.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated the workflow on 37 graph and labelled-transition-system algorithms, including the Hopcroft–Tarjan triconnectivity test, and report that many verifications took hours to a few days.
watch_item: Machine-checked proofs still depend on appropriate specifications, so correctness-critical decisions require human review.
